passA.name: Content-stream / optical-content-group reconstruction
method: A hand-written PDF content-stream interpreter tokenises the page stream and tracks the graphics and text state (q/Q/cm, BT/ET, Tm/Td/TD/T*, Tf, Tc/Tw/Tz, Tj/TJ).

The 23 /OC /MCn BDC ... EMC marked-content blocks map one-to-one onto the issuer's own optical content groups, so every glyph is attributed to an issuer-defined layer exactly. Floor identity comes from the layer name (3F番号 / 5F番号 / 7F番号), not from geometry.
Glyph advances are computed from the PDF's own /Widths arrays (TT0/TT1) and /DW (C0_0/C0_1), giving each glyph an exact device-space origin and extent.

Glyphs are projected onto their own text direction, clustered onto baselines, split into digit runs and dot-leader runs by the residual gap after each glyph's advance, and grouped into printed segments at along-baseline gaps. The gap distribution is cleanly bimodal: at most 1.7 pt inside a printed label, at least 7.4 pt between segments.
Row numbers come from the issuer's own 3F列 / 5F列 / 7F列 marker labels, mapped onto baselines by piecewise-linear interpolation between markers.
passA.reproducibility: Re-run from scratch after Pass B was corrected; the output file is byte-identical (SHA-256 d4b28c23a2ab7721474132f90963346766078f8c984a66c9097a3a528664266e).

passB.name: Rendered row-band reconstruction
passB.acquisition: an independent second fetch of the same URL, verified to the same SHA-256
method: Text geometry comes from pdfplumber / pdfminer.six — a different library and a different parser from Pass A's hand-written interpreter. No optical content group is consulted.

The page is rendered to a raster; the printed seat bars are recovered as connected components of the bar colours after filling the white glyph holes, yielding 1,253 bars (748 purple, 490 blue, 15 pink) of the chart's 5.1 pt stroke width.

Floors are identified from the chart's own tinted background panels, each panel NAMED by the GATE numbers printed inside it (101-104 / 301-304 / 501-512 / 701-712). This gave 220 bars on 1F, 320 on 3F, 285 on 5F and 428 on 7F.

Pairing is by rendered row band, not by gap threshold: one bar carries one printed range, and its two numbers are read off the bar's two ends in the glyphs' own text direction. A bar with no dot leaders is split at its widest internal glyph gap.
Row numbers are obtained by COUNTING rendered bands between the issuer's printed row markers, and the count between each marker pair must equal the markers' own numeric difference.
Traversal is deliberately reversed: floors 7F -> 5F -> 3F, blocks right to left.

declaredDiscontinuities.meaning: the 5F centre has no rows 4-5; the balcony band ends at row 3 and the main centre stand starts at row 6

passB.correctedDuringWork: The first Pass B run derived each bar's axis from a principal-component fit whose sign is arbitrary, so some numbers were read right-to-left (28 as 82, 169-188 as 802-981). The machine comparison caught it immediately. The pairing logic was corrected to read along the glyphs' own text direction and Pass B was regenerated; Pass A was untouched and re-verified byte-identical. No value from either pass was ever reconciled by hand.

comparison.structuralFeatures: Split segments, internal gaps, truncated rows and the two-seat printed pairs are identical in both passes; the 80 rows carrying internal gaps have identical gap structure.
comparison.wheelchairUnnumberedAreas: Both passes independently return no numbered identifier anywhere inside the 3F ACCESSIBLE SEATING platform, and both return the same truncated block ends beside it.
comparison.vipAndFirstFloor: Neither pass produced any 1F or VIP identifier inside the registered scope; Pass A excludes them by layer, Pass B by background panel and GATE numbering.

visualAudit.method: The PDF was re-rendered from the vector source at high scale; for each printed row every section was clipped, deskewed to its own text direction and cropped to a legible strip, then read directly against the matched table.
visualAudit.coverage: 100% of the printed rows — all 83 (floor, row) keys: 3F rows 1-29, 5F rows 1-26, 7F rows 1-28. Every section of every row was read, so every split range, every internal gap, every truncated row and every block's ordinary rows were covered rather than sampled.

reconciliation.relationTo20033: The issuer publishes 座席数：20,033席 on /floor/ as the whole-venue figure; it includes LEVEL1 アリーナ, which is issuer-declared performance-dependent and excluded here, and it is not a 3F/5F/7F subtotal. The difference was NOT closed, explained away, or used to add or remove any seat.
reconciliation.expectedSeatCountRationale: The issuer publishes no 3F, 5F or 7F subtotal anywhere in the current material, so no nominal upper-level subtotal exists to record. expectedSeatCount is left null rather than inventing one; scope.exactSubtotal carries the mapped count 15,929 as the fixed-only contract requires.

accessibilityVipSemantics.wheelchair: wheelchairSemantics.status = not-reflected with accessibilityConversionNotReflected = true. The PDF's 車椅子 layer draws the 3F ACCESSIBLE SEATING platform with no printed row or seat number, and the issuer's FAQ routes wheelchair seating to each event organiser with 「鑑賞エリアのレイアウトは公演により異なります。」. No seat ID, position or replacement relation was created.
accessibilityVipSemantics.vip: Excluded as a non-public area on the issuer's own statement 「ご契約者専用フロアです。一般の方のご入場・ご利用はできません。」; the VIP layer carries no printed seat numbers.
accessibilityVipSemantics.firstFloor: Excluded as an issuer-declared performance-dependent area. No 1F identifier appears anywhere in the registered set.

runtimeIdentity.reason: Seat numbers and row numbers repeat across 3F, 5F and 7F, so each floor has its own areaId and the runtime key (area, row, seat) cannot collide. The balcony is separated because the issuer draws it on its own layer, in its own colour, under its own printed caption 「バルコニー席 / BALCONY SEATING」.
runtimeIdentity.noInventedBlockNames: The issuer names no individual seating block, so no block name was created. Only the issuer's printed floor, row and seat numbers identify a seat; the area labels reuse the issuer's own level-stand names and are disclosed as display-only organising names.
